rows.claim: RosterEntry has fields id::DeviceId, cell::StagingCell, claims::NTuple{N,String}, schema::Schema
rows.evidence: src/roster.jl:254 (fields dev, id::Int, drain::Function, should_abort, account, handle); no DeviceId, Schema or claims field. Cell, claims and schema live on handle.writer (src/dataplane.jl:372)
rows.fix: Show the real struct: `dev::AbstractDevice`, `id::Int`, `drain::Function` (the compiled cell+scatter thunk), `should_abort::Bool`, `account::WriterAccount`, `handle::Any`; say the cell, claim (as `writer.faces`) and schema ride on the handle's compiled `Writer` (D-261).
rows.note: Later log entry D-261 records the handle holding the writer.

rows.claim: the entry's id is stable across runs and is the trace tag
rows.evidence: src/roster.jl:254 id::Int; trace tags are the who string, e.g. "device 1 (Pad)" (probe:37; src/trace.jl:82 comment says tags are _who(entry) and "harness"). The id is stable (src/sim.jl:2525 plane.next_id, never reused), but it is not the tag.
rows.fix: `id::Int  # stable across runs; the trace tags the writer by its name "device <id> (<Type>)"`.

rows.claim: attach! validates face names (AttachUnknownFace) first, then admits through identity and claims, then compiles
rows.evidence: src/sim.jl:2510-2530: identity check runs before _claim, so an already-attached device with an unknown face gets AlreadyAttached (probe:42); AttachUnknownFace comes between identity and ClaimConflict (probe:44).
rows.fix: Order the sentence as identity (`AlreadyAttached`), then face validation (`AttachUnknownFace`), then claims (`ClaimConflict`), then compile the staging shape and add the entry.
rows.note: Spec 11.3 text (design/spec.md:8324) states the unknown-face refusal without an order; test_roster.jl:73 asserts identity first.

rows.evidence: A bare NamedTuple is not an AbstractBinding (src/roster.jl:60); the shipped table binding is `TableBinding(; entries...)` (src/bindings.jl:60, claims at 94). Entry vocabulary face/deadzone/expo is correct.

rows.claim: mutable struct StagingCell with `@atomic pending::Union{Nothing, Batch}`
rows.evidence: src/dataplane.jl:25: `mutable struct StagingCell{B}` with `@atomic pending::Union{Nothing,Base.RefValue{B}}`; the batch rides boxed in a Ref for one pointer-width CAS (docstring dataplane.jl:15-24).
rows.fix: `mutable struct StagingCell{B}; @atomic pending::Union{Nothing,Base.RefValue{B}}; end  # the latest not-yet-applied batch, boxed so each handoff is one atomic pointer`.

rows.claim: map_input(datum, binding) returns the NamedTuple `(throttle = 0.70, elevator = -0.05)`
rows.evidence: src/bindings.jl:102-125: map_input returns a tuple of `"face" => value` pairs, one per datum field, and the datum is keyed by channel (stick_y), not face. Same form at lines 232 (`(flaps = 0.5,)`) and 263.
rows.fix: Write `# ⇒ ("throttle" => 0.70, "elevator" => -0.05)` (pairs, as `stage!` takes them); likewise `("flaps" => 0.5,)` at line 232 and the staged pairs at line 263.

rows.claim: the cells and scatters form a known tuple the frame function specializes on, with no dynamic dispatch at frame top
rows.evidence: src/sim.jl:2672-2675: the drain iterates the roster Vector and calls `entry.drain()::Bool`, a thunk held in a `Function` field (src/roster.jl:254), so each entry costs one dynamic call; src/roster.jl:278-281 says this iteration is used in place of tuple specialization.
rows.fix: Say the roster is fixed at `run!`, so the cells and scatters could form a known tuple the frame function specializes on; the code instead iterates the roster, one dynamic call per entry, with each scatter compiled concretely at the stopped-sim point.
rows.note: Spec design/spec.md:8683-8690 carries the same wording but calls the specialization 'an implementation freedom ... not an obligation' and licenses iterating a roster array.

rows.claim: the trace's header holds the initial state, root-input values and per-writer schemas
rows.evidence: src/trace.jl:78-83: header is a `Checkpoint` (state, frame, boundary; src/checkpoint.jl:106) and the per-writer schemas are the separate `schemas` field of `Trace`; root-input values sit inside the checkpoint state's table.
rows.fix: ...plus the header (the opening checkpoint: state, root-input values in its table, frame and boundary) and the trace's `schemas` list of per-writer face names.

rows.claim: replay feeds the same batches to the same drain
rows.evidence: src/sim.jl:2656-2660, 2690-2720: under replay `drain!` returns `_replay_drain!`, a separate path that discards live cells and applies compiled feed records (D-274). The loop is the same, the drain is a substituted path.
rows.fix: Replay feeds the recorded batches through the ordinary loop, with the drain's one substitution reading the trace instead of the cells, and gets a bit-identical trajectory.

rows.claim: Two warning kinds cover the violations: OutOfClaimEntry is a device-surface violation, ClaimedFaceEntry the harness violation 'and only that'
rows.evidence: src/dataplane.jl:424-431: a harness `stage!` naming a face that is no root input also gives OutOfClaimEntry (probe:33, face :nope, incumbent nothing); stage! docstring src/sim.jl:2609-2611 records it.
rows.fix: Add that a harness `stage!` naming no root input at all is also `OutOfClaimEntry` (no incumbent); `ClaimedFaceEntry` stays the harness's kind for a claimed face.
rows.note: Spec design/spec.md:16035-16039 says ClaimedFaceEntry is 'Harness writer only' and does not restrict OutOfClaimEntry; the doc agrees with the spec on ClaimedFaceEntry.

rows.claim: OutOfClaimEntry payload includes the writer id
rows.evidence: src/diagnostics.jl:1602-1607: fields are face, value, surface (the claim set) and incumbent; no writer id. The writer is known from whose cell and status record carry it (probe:30).
rows.fix: Face, discarded value, the claim set, and the incumbent's id when the face is claimed elsewhere; the writer is named by the status record that carries it.
rows.note: Spec design/spec.md:16040-16042 lists the same four fields without a writer id, agreeing with the code.

rows.evidence: src/devices.jl:518-524, 514: liveness is baked by the GUI device's own `port_views(handle)` call at its loop top after the freeze; run! (src/sim.jl:1628-1655) bakes nothing.
rows.fix: `run!` reads the roster and spawns the GUI task, whose loop bakes widget liveness once with `port_views` ([§11.7]), and the drain was specialized at the last stopped-sim point.
rows.note: Spec design/spec.md:8301 says liveness is 'baked once at run start', consistent with this at run granularity.

rows.evidence: src/roster.jl:431-441: drain thunks are compiled in `_install_writers!`, called from `attach!`, `detach!` and the doors `init!`, `restore!`, `replay!` (src/sim.jl:703), never from `run!`.
rows.fix: ...the drain was specialized when the roster last changed or a door (`init!`, `restore!`, `replay!`) opened the run.
